standard_prerequisites: the tableau derivation relation Gamma proves A as defined in this unit
consistency of a set of sentences defined by absence of a closed tableau
tableaus grow from a finite initial list of signed formulas
core_obligations: Prove both directions of compactness for tableaus: (1) if Gamma proves A then a finite subset Gamma_0 proves A; (2) if every finite subset of Gamma is consistent then Gamma is consistent
proof_roadmap: A closed tableau is by definition grown from a finite initial list of signed formulas, so a derivation of A from Gamma uses only finitely many premises B_1,...,B_n; the same closed tableau witnesses Gamma_0 proves A
If Gamma is inconsistent there is a closed tableau from the list of all members of Gamma; its finite initial list is a finite subset Gamma_0 whose closed tableau shows Gamma_0 inconsistent
Contraposing (2) gives: if every finite subset is consistent then Gamma is consistent
difficulty_reason: Both clauses follow from the finiteness of a tableau's initial list given the unit's definitions; formally H1, kept at H2 by the difficulty scale.
